svg.text: auto-indexing OFF on the inputs — the seed is computed from i
FALSE: refnum straight across, error straight across
THE SHIFT REGISTERS ARE THE WHOLE POINT. The socket and the error cluster leave the loop
body on the RIGHT border and re-enter on the LEFT on the next iteration. Unit 5 therefore runs
on whatever socket unit 4 left behind — including a brand-new one the Case Structure just opened.
Wire a shift register only ONE side and the loop still compiles — it just silently reuses the
initial value forever. That is the single most common shift-register bug and it looks like a DUT fault.
A CONDITIONAL tunnel (TT1, TT2) has a small condition terminal under it: only iterations whose
condition is TRUE contribute an element. That is how tester errors are counted separately from
unit failures — availability and FPY are different numbers and must never be computed from one array.
Clear Errors sits between Sequencer and the case so the loop keeps running. Without it the error
rides the shift register into every later iteration and the whole batch reports the same failure.
The socket is CHAINED through the golden-unit gate into SR1, never branched off TCP Open — same
rule as Compare_OCV. TCP Close after the loop reads SR1’s RIGHT-side output, so it closes the
socket that is actually live, not the one opened at the start.
FALSE case: both tunnels wired straight across, nothing else
